questions.context: In a festival in Valledupar, musicians play an accordion, a drum and a guitar.

options.feedback: The accordion, the drum and the guitar are all instruments.
Table, chair and lamp are furniture, not instruments.
Mango, papaya and banana are fruits, not instruments.
Bus, taxi and moto are transport, not instruments.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta presenta vocabulario básico de instrumentos en inglés. También se conecta cada instrumento con el festival vallenato.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Barranquilla, dancers move to cumbia during the carnival parade.

options.feedback: Food is what people eat, not movements with music.
Animals are living beings, not movements with music.

options.text: Movements of the body with music.
options.feedback: A dance is body movement that follows the rhythm of music.
Cars are transport machines, not movements with music.

questions.explanation: La palabra dance significa movimientos del cuerpo con música. También se comprende con la cumbia del carnaval barranquillero.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Sincelejo, a boy says: "They _____ cumbia in the school festival."

options.feedback: "Dances" is singular and does not agree with the plural they.
"Danced" is past tense and the festival is happening now.
"Dance" agrees with the plural subject they in the present.
"Dancing" needs am, is or are and is not correct alone here.

questions.explanation: El presente simple usa la forma base con they en afirmativo. También se practica con la cumbia del festival escolar sincelejano.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Riohacha, students read: "The vallenato concert starts at 5 p.m. The cumbia show starts at 7 p.m. The fireworks close the night at 9 p.m."

options.feedback: The vallenato concert starts at 5 p.m., not 7 p.m.
The text says the cumbia show starts at 7 p.m.
The fireworks close the night at 9 p.m., not 7 p.m.
The text never mentions a food fair.

questions.explanation: Leer programas exige ubicar cada evento en su hora exacta. También se aplica con una fiesta musical en Riohacha.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word means the opposite of loud?
questions.context: At home in Popayán, a girl listens: "The drum sounds loud. The flute sounds soft. The guitar sounds sweet."

options.feedback: Noisy means the same as loud, not the opposite.
Soft is the opposite of loud and describes the flute.
Strong describes power, not the opposite of loud.
Fast describes speed, not the volume of sound.

questions.explanation: Los opuestos como loud y soft describen el volumen del sonido. También se asocian con instrumentos que escuchan los niños en casa.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you conclude about vallenato and bambuco?
questions.context: In Ocaña, a program says: "Vallenato uses accordion and drums. Bambuco uses guitar and tiple. Both styles make people dance."

options.text: Both use exactly the same instruments.
options.feedback: Vallenato uses accordion while bambuco uses guitar and tiple.
The program says both styles make people dance.

options.text: They use different instruments but share the same effect.
options.feedback: The instruments differ, yet both rhythms make people dance.
Vallenato and bambuco are traditional Colombian rhythms.

questions.explanation: Analizar programas permite comparar instrumentos y efectos de cada ritmo. También se trabaja el contraste entre dos estilos colombianos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Montería, a teacher compares: "Listen to the drums!" and "She listens to the drums."

options.text: The first gives an order, the second describes a person.
options.feedback: "Listen" without subject orders, while "she listens" describes.
Only the first sentence without subject is an imperative.
Both sentences are in the present, not in the past.

options.text: The first describes a person, the second gives an order.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed; the imperative has no subject.

questions.explanation: El imperativo omite el sujeto para ordenar y el presente lo incluye para describir. También se practica con los tambores del Sinú.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which group is the best for the carnival?
questions.context: In Pasto, two carnival groups appear: one plays traditional music with safe sound and organized parade; the other plays extremely loud music at midnight near a hospital.

options.text: The midnight group, because hospitals enjoy loud music.
options.feedback: Loud music at midnight near a hospital harms sick people.

options.text: The organized parade with safe sound.
options.feedback: An organized parade with safe sound respects everyone.

options.text: The loudest group, because louder is always better.
options.feedback: Extremely loud music damages ears and bothers neighbors.

options.text: Both groups are equal for the party.
options.feedback: The groups are very different; only one respects the community.

questions.explanation: Evaluar grupos implica revisar volumen seguro y respeto por la comunidad. También se promueve disfrutar el carnaval sin dañar los oídos.
questions.subject: ingles
